lines: I.  Introduction

Fig. 1.  The compatibility problem. A frozen learned fleet saves fuel against its own base driver under fixed-time signals; after the upgrade to a learned signal its benefit is exactly zero with no timing, and the old timing served as SPaT harms it.

Learned traffic signals and learned connected-vehicle fleets are owned by different parties and upgraded on different schedules. A fleet trained against fixed-time signals uses the broadcast signal phase and timing (SPaT) as a plan; a learned adaptive signal decides every few seconds, so the plan disappears.

THE LOSS IS REAL. In SUMO on a 16-signal grid, a PPO eco-driving fleet that saves 6.5% fuel against its base driver loses that benefit when the signals are upgraded. A forecast of the learned signal costs the fleet's own vehicles time, and light-side commitments cost more than they recover.
THE QUESTION. Can the fleet's benefit be recovered WITHOUT retraining either population, by changing only what the fleet is told and what the signal sees?
What the literature leaves open

SPaT prediction for adaptive signals (statistical residual-time and supervised time-to-green models) changes only the forecast; eco-driving under uncertain timing changes the vehicle; joint signal–vehicle control and FoRL (2026), which trains a signal to forecast its own actions, retrain one side. None keeps both learned populations frozen.

Self-defeating forecasts are not new in transportation: anticipatory route guidance can invalidate its own forecast, and consistent guidance is a fixed point. The new instance is at the signal–eco-driving interface, where the fleet's reaction passes through a learned signal's observation.
II.  Methodology

Fig. 2.  The two frozen populations and the two interfaces TSI changes (blue). The orange path is the closed loop: published timing changes the approach, a halting-count signal does not see slow cars as demand, holds its greens, and the forecast's target shifts.

STAGED, REGISTERED DESIGN. M1 a fleet worth protecting; M2 the upgrade removes its benefit, measured as a difference in differences; M3 repair through the interfaces only; M4 transfer. Every experiment had a written protocol before its code ran, a smoke run, and self-checks that can fail.

II.  Methodology, continued

WHY ONE SIDE IS NOT ENOUGH, PROVED. A threshold signal fed by an arrival stream at rate λ, of which a fleet share ρ glides and is weighted A, is served after T; a forecast learned without the fleet predicts T₀ and errs by

The light-side half is needed exactly when the signal's input weights gliding vehicles below halted ones, and the error grows with the fleet share; with n vehicles a halting count misses with probability at least pⁿ, while A ≥ 1 never misses. Machine-checked in Lean 4: four modules, 32 audited declarations, standard axioms only, no sorry.

THE THEOREM PREDICTS THE SIGN OF EVERY MEASURED GREEN CHANGE: lengthening for the halting-count learned signal (15.0 → 17.1 s), none for MaxPressure, which counts every vehicle (18.1 → 18.0 s), and a return to baseline under TSI.
III.  Results
Fig. 3.  TSI against the no-SPaT fallback in every registered test (95% intervals; verdicts at each test's level).

CONFIRMED AND REPLICATED. Registered second attempt: −3.85% agent fuel [3.26, 4.43] with every time loss within +0.5 s/veh (one-sided α = 0.025). It held on fresh traffic (−3.70%) and with two independently trained sets of signals and fleets recalibrated from scratch (−2.61%, −2.97%). Each half alone failed every time.
ONE SETTING FOR EVERY SIGNAL. (A, B) = (1, 0.5), fixed on other signals, met every limit on unseen policies (−2.88%), removing the per-site grid search.
ROBUSTNESS. Within the limits with 80% detection, 1 m/s speed noise and 20% SPaT loss; a 1-s latency removes most of the saving.

COMPARATORS. Against retraining the fleet, TSI's time losses are lower and fuel non-inferiority at 0.5 pp is not shown. A corrected DC-Ada port tuned at TSI's budget, on fresh traffic, saves similar fuel (−3.45%) but adds 2.87 s/veh to the fleet's time loss and fails the limits; TSI's time losses are lower (−3.15 s/veh), fuel is not ordered.
IV.  Discussion

Fig. 4.  Mechanism. Under the service the learned signal holds its greens longer (A); the residual time cost grows with that lengthening (B); on a replayed schedule exact timing saves fuel and time (C).

A PUBLISHED SIGNAL CONFIRMS THE MECHANISM. Registered in advance: with MaxPressure, which counts vehicles at every speed, the fleet-side service alone meets every limit (−2.68% fuel), the case the theorem says needs no light-side change.

WHEN IT TRANSFERS. Served-answer diagnostics (exact on all three networks): on one-lane spider, publication shifts the forecast by +7.8 s and commanded agents hold five times as many humans; spider rebuilt with two lanes passes; a refitted forecaster removes the shift but not the failure. rand3 passes a second attempt with a wider adapter range.
Limitations — what is not established
Simulation only. The fuel saving under learned signals holds for HBEFA4 but not PHEMlight5 (the fleet's own fixed-time benefit survives both); the frozen design does not transfer to IDM drivers.
Fails on one-lane roads with enough following traffic; three synthetic networks are not a sample of real cities; the theorem predicts signs, not magnitudes.
V.  Conclusions

Two learned populations that each work alone can stop working together when one is upgraded, invisibly to either population's inputs. Neither interface alone repairs it; both together recover most of the benefit, without retraining either population.
For a practitioner: before upgrading signals a learned fleet relies on, ask whether the signal's input sees the fleet's slower approach and whether the road lets followers pass.
How the numbers were produced

REGISTERED, THEN RUN. Every experiment was registered before its code ran, smoke-tested end to end, and reported as it came out, failures included. Runs are deterministic; reports refuse incomplete panels; parity, identity and exactness self-checks gate every result.

CORRECTED IN THE OPEN. Two of our own claims were withdrawn after an independent audit of code and raw rows (a DC-Ada port with mismatched tuning horizons; a non-comparable forecast-error sample) and replaced by corrected runs.
